intelligence.human_view: A control that does nothing when you touch it is a picture of a control — and a picture cannot be operated by a child or a grandma. The touch is the proof: you touch it, you feel it push in and out, it lights up, it moves, it does stuff. That is the best — because pressing is useful, helpful, and obvious, all three at once: useful because it does something, helpful because it shows you it did, obvious because anyone can see how. The bar is the person, not the control: an internet all children and grandmas can operate. If a child cannot press it and a grandma cannot feel it, it is not done. This sharpens the 3D press law (SN-3181) into a test anyone can run: touch it — did you feel it? If not, it failed, however beautiful it is. And it answers the Smart Mail eye's caution from 22:50Z once and for all: a rule in bytes that produces no visible press change is not a press at all.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine a button that does nothing when you press it — it just sits there, flat and quiet. That is not a real button. A real button pushes in when you touch it, lights up, moves, and does something — and you can FEEL it. That is the best button. And if a little kid and a grandma can both press it easily, then it is a perfect button.
intelligence.grandma_view: Dear, when you touch something on the screen, you should feel it — it pushes in and out, it lights up, it moves, it does something. That is the best. Pressing should be useful, and helpful, and obvious — so obvious that a little child and a grandma can both use it without anyone having to explain. An internet that children and grandmas can operate — that is the bar.
intelligence.naya_view: YOU TOUCH IT, YOU FEEL IT — IT PUSHES IN AND OUT, IT LIGHTS UP, IT MOVES, IT DOES STUFF. THAT IS THE BEST. PRESSING IS USEFUL, HELPFUL AND OBVIOUS. AN INTERNET ALL CHILDREN AND GRANDMAS CAN OPERATE.
